planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Kismet Raspberry was bred to flower heavily from seed in its first year, unlike many older coneflowers that need a full season to establish before blooming well.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Kismet Raspberry is part of the Kismet coneflower series bred by Darwin Perennials for a compact, uniform, heavily branched habit and the ability to flower strongly the same year from an early sowing, a trait many older Echinacea cultivars lack. Its bright raspberry-pink, sun-facing blooms with a prominent orange-brown cone open over a long summer window and draw a steady stream of butterflies and bees. Deadhead spent flowers to extend bloom, or leave some seed heads standing into fall and winter as a food source for goldfinches. Once established it is drought-tolerant and easy-care, needing division only every three to four years if flowering starts to decline.

common_name: Kismet Intense Orange Coneflower (First-Year-Flowering Compact Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; like other Kismet coneflowers, Intense Orange flowers heavily from an early sowing in its first year rather than needing a season to establish.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Kismet Intense Orange bears vivid, saturated orange blooms on a compact, heavily branched plant, part of the Kismet series bred for strong first-year flowering and a tidier habit than many older coneflower cultivars. The bold color reads well from a distance and holds up through summer heat, while the wide, flat blooms make an easy landing pad for butterflies and bees. Deadheading extends the bloom season, though leaving some seed heads through fall and winter provides food for goldfinches and other seed-eating birds. It is drought-tolerant once established and rarely needs division except to renew an aging clump every few years.

common_name: Bandana Cherry Lantana (Compact Mounding Red-Pink Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; avoid overwatering, since lantana is highly drought-tolerant once established and prone to root problems in soggy soil.

directions: Bandana Cherry bears dense, rounded flower clusters that open bright cherry-red and pink and shift tone slightly as they age, giving the two-tone effect typical of the genus, on the same compact, uniform, mounding habit that defines the Bandana lantana series. It flowers nonstop from spring through frost with no deadheading required and is a heavy draw for butterflies throughout the season. Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, since lantana tolerates heat, drought, and poor soil far better than excess moisture. In zone 9 it typically dies back to the ground in a hard freeze and resprouts from the roots the following spring once established for a season or more.
sources: Proven Winners — Bandana lantana series notes

common_name: Bandana Rose Lantana (Compact Mounding Pink-Yellow Bicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; avoid overwatering, since lantana is highly drought-tolerant once established and prone to root problems in soggy soil.

directions: Bandana Rose produces rounded flower clusters that combine rosy-pink outer florets with a golden-yellow center, a soft bicolor blend that stands out from the hotter oranges and reds of many landscape lantana. It shares the Bandana series' compact, dense, mounding habit and blooms continuously from spring through frost without deadheading, drawing butterflies steadily through the season. Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun, since excess moisture causes root problems far more often than drought does in this genus. In the coldest winters within its range it dies to the ground and returns from the roots the following spring once its root system is well established.
sources: Proven Winners — Bandana lantana series notes

common_name: Luscious Citrus Blend Lantana (Compact Trailing Multicolor Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost date in well-drained soil in full sun; its low, spreading habit suits hanging baskets and container edges as well as garden beds.

directions: Luscious Citrus Blend mixes yellow, orange, and pink florets in the same flower cluster, echoing the color-shifting look of old-fashioned lantana on the lower, more mounding and trailing habit that defines the Luscious series. Flowers are held steadily over the foliage from spring through frost with no deadheading needed, and the citrus-toned clusters draw butterflies and bees throughout the long bloom season. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date; like other modern lantana selections it is highly heat- and drought-tolerant once established and performs best when allowed to dry between waterings. In zone 9 it usually dies back to the roots in a hard freeze and resprouts vigorously the following spring from an established root system.
sources: Proven Winners — Luscious lantana series notes
